title: Paul DeDroit, Johnny DeDroit and homesick musicians
summary: Lopez talks about Paul and Johnny DeDroit, Johnny's carnival band and a trumpeter who went home before a radio job.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Oh, I was gonna ask one of the questions about, um, if there are many more people from New Orleans out here that you can think of, like this Paul DeGroix, did you know him?
Yeah, I knew Paul very well. His brother Johnny's got a, they say, got a very fine band on there.
Well, yes, he's still there.
Now, Johnny plays all the carnival balls. Mm-hmm, yeah.

And, uh, about a year or so ago, they were playing out at, uh, the lake at the Pontchartrain, where Mildenburg used to be, in Eastman Park. Is, uh, Paul DeGroix lives out in Hollywood, I believe. He lives in North Hollywood.
North Hollywood. Yeah, he lives out near Miller's.
Not far from Dussleville.
Yeah, he, Paul's over at the Fox Studios. Mm-hmm. And Paul's a very fine drummer. Yes, I know.
I've never met him, though.
Yeah, very, very fine. Very fine, legitimate drummer. He's a good dance drummer.
He still works as a, uh, is he, uh, quite a bit younger than you, or about the same age now?
The guy looks, he's got, he's got a mop of hair on him. He looks, uh, I, I'll say, I don't know. I, I'm proud in 69. Mm-hmm. I bet that Paul's over 60, 63, something like that.
Yeah, I'm only got it.
The guy looks like he's 40.
Mm-hmm.
Really? He's still got that pep and life and stuff. He jumps around.
Yeah.
Good for a million laughs. Mm-hmm. Yeah, he, he's, apparently. And Johnny, I, I saw Johnny, we were down in 52, and Johnny hasn't changed a day since I knew him.
Mm-hmm.

And I remember when Johnny was playing in the scene of the old, which he was with a little pair of white pants on in front of the big band at the lake. Yeah. Yeah, I remember that. And, uh, I was up to see Paul, the mother, Mrs. Detroit. But Paul gets all the big French up with the big carnival balls now. Yeah. I mean, Johnny does.
Yeah, for Johnny.

Well, he, Johnny is a very fine school musician, see? Mm-hmm. And, well, he had an experience. He came out here, too. So, I got him lined up in the, in the radio station. And, it was just around Thanksgiving time. And, we had, we were all playing for a nice great big dinner. For Johnny, see? Yeah. And, uh, Johnny's all set to open up at this big radio station. And, I three-sheeted him all over the town. What a fine trumpet player was. And, he is. And, uh, there comes the, the Thanksgiving dinner, little Johnny. So, then, the studio calls me. Yeah. He says, hey, what happened to that, that, that kid you, you, from New Orleans, that wizard you're talking about? I said, I want to know. I said, of course, we got a great big Thanksgiving dinner waiting. He's waiting for him. That damn fool went back home.
That's quick, huh? Some of these guys get lonesome. Couldn't, couldn't take it. They're homesick and they can't take it.
